spec.summary: Add six new attack storylines (ransomware, insider_exfil, phishing_bec, cloud_iam_abuse, supply_chain_ci, ot_opcua_sabotage) in the existing ScenarioDef + oracle_<name>.yaml + scenario_registry pattern, plus a generated ATT&CK technique matrix (eval/attack/technique_matrix.py). The matrix shows technique x rule-exists / fires-on-storyline / survives-mutation, and its gate fails when any rule or technique is unexercised by every storyline. Today 16 of 35 rules are in no oracle, so the gate would be red on landing, and all 16 become reachable. The storylines add 34 real-parsed steps. Where no rule exists, a step becomes an honest gap with an ATT&CK technique id and a reason. The only MISSING-rule gaps are listed per storyline below, and no rules are invented. Oracles are authored from the rule descriptions and parser docstrings before the pipeline is run on them. A small number of harness changes are required: adapter coverage for the new sources, three new mutation variants, additive fired_pairs in the matrix rows, a step_dependencies oracle key, and must_not_fire / campaign_membership checks in the reconciler. No rule, parser, WS-8 promotion or contract is changed.
spec.approach:
I read SSOT.md rows 17-18, eval/twin/{scenario,scenarios_extra,scenario_registry,oracle_consistency,report}.py, eval/adversarial/{mutate_generic,scenario_matrix,evasion_search,layer_a}.py, eval/attack/{coverage_layer,fire_check}.py, all 35 contracts/rules/*.yml and the parsers. I ran only read-only checks: the three existing storylines were graded, and one parse-only smoke of the new payload shapes ran through ws2.normalize_one from the scratchpad. No rule-firing was observed for any new storyline, and every expectation below comes from rule descriptions and parser docstrings.

== 0. What exists and the gap ==
- scenario.ScenarioDef(name, steps, build, oracle_path, summary, decoy, decoy_steps) and scenario_registry.ALL hold 3 storylines. oracle_consistency.reconcile(seed, sdef), scenario_matrix.run_scenario and evasion_search.search_scenario iterate reg.ALL, so each new ScenarioDef is gated there automatically.
- I counted rules named in expected_rules of the three oracles. 19 of 35 rule files are covered, so 16 are in no oracle and are exercised by no storyline:
  - agent_destructive_command, agent_tool_call_burst, bank_db_priv_esc, bank_mass_card_read
  - common_after_hours_admin, common_beaconing, common_bruteforce_sourceless, common_impossible_travel
  - common_password_spray, common_rapid_account_lifecycle
  - ot_config_change, ot_modbus_unauthorized_write_ticketed, ot_new_device_on_segment, ot_new_engineering_connection, ot_opcua_write_unauthorized_node, ot_write_outside_maintenance
- agent_tool_call_burst carries no mitre: block at all (deliberate, per the repo).
- eval/attack/coverage_layer.py (declared coverage) and fire_check.py (fires on its own fixture) already exist. The new matrix adds the missing third and fourth columns, fires-end-to-end-on-a-storyline and survives-mutation, and reuses coverage_layer.load_rules rather than re-parsing rules.
- mutate_generic adapters are only complete for the existing sources:
  - get/set_src_ip lack cef, db_audit, opcua_audit, sysmon and inventory_diff.
  - get/set_actor lack sysmon, db_audit, opcua_audit and cef.
  - set_time does not rewrite db_audit "timestamp", inventory_diff "seen_at" or k8s "requestReceivedTimestamp" (the k8s parser prefers that field over meta.received_at, so shift_* on infra_takeover's k8s step may be a silent partial no-op today).
- _BASE_MS = 1751500000000 is Wed 2025-07-02 23:46:40 UTC, outside 08:00-18:00. Every existing storyline therefore runs at night, so time-of-day rules are never shown going silent.

== 1. Oracle authoring protocol (applies to all six) ==
1. Write oracle_<name>.yaml first, from the rule's description: and detection: block plus the parser docstring only. Each file begins with a provenance: block (authored date, "pipeline not run", and a sha256 per rule file read, hashed over the normalised description+detection+siem blocks). test_storylines_wide asserts the hashes still match, so a later rule change forces a re-review of the oracle. Provenance cannot be mechanically proven; the commit-order convention (oracle before builder) is process only.
2. Schema is the existing one (expected_sequence, sequence_constraints, allowed_relationships, detection_points, severity_band, evidence, incident_membership). Four additive optional keys, all read only by oracle_consistency and the matrix, so report.py is untouched:
   - detection_points.<step>.must_not_fire: [rule ids]. A built-in negative control; a forbidden rule firing is a new finding kind.
   - detection_points.<step>.gap.attack_technique: "T...". Mandatory whenever no_rule_exists is true. It feeds the matrix "demonstrated but undetected" table.
   - detection_points.<step>.context: true, plus a top-level step_dependencies: {step: [steps]}. For benign enabling telemetry such as the victim's own earlier login. scenario_matrix excludes dependent steps from the loss/collateral rule, because dropping the victim login legitimately blinds impossible-travel.
   - campaign_membership: {campaign_count: 1, full_coverage: true}. Graded by oracle_consistency from the existing grade keys campaign_count and campaign_full_coverage.
3. Pivoting storylines and the ratified WS-8 invariant (ADR-009/010: tracks never merge). The oracles set incident_membership.incident_count honestly (the number of single-entity tracks that really can span the whole chain, which is 0 or 1) and put the cross-entity "one campaign" expectation in campaign_membership via the read-side link_campaigns view. No oracle asks WS-8 to merge tracks. Whether campaign_count == 1 becomes a blocking target is an owner decision (listed below).
4. First-run disagreements are findings, not edits. A decorative, unexpected, stale-gap or forbidden-rule finding is fixed in the product or recorded in oracle_consistency._ACCEPTED with a dated reason. It is never tuned away in the oracle.
5. Timestamps come from datetime(...).timestamp() as in negative_controls._epoch_ms, never wall clock. Per-storyline ingest-id tags are unique. Documentation-range IPs (RFC 5737) and .invalid / example domains only. The geoip sample map is 203.0.113.0/24=RU, 198.51.100.0/24=CN, 192.0.2.0/24=US, 2001:db8::/32=DE.

== 2. The six storylines ==
Seeds vary STRUCTURE (counts, addresses, accounts, hosts, names, sessions), never only identifiers, via Random(seed*prime+c) exactly as scenarios_extra does. Counts are kept above rule thresholds with margin and below the next rule's threshold wherever the oracle uses must_not_fire.

== 3. Missing-rule register (honest gaps, no rule invented) ==
- ransomware: T1078 (foothold logon), T1490 (shadow-copy delete), T1490 (cloud snapshot wipe), T1486 (mass file encryption).
- insider_exfil: T1560.001, T1074.001, T1567, T1070.
- phishing_bec: T1566.001 (no mail parser), T1204.002, T1114.003 (no M365 audit parser), T1565.001.
- cloud_iam_abuse: T1110.004 (cross-source blind spot), T1087.004, T1098.001, T1562.008.
- supply_chain_ci: T1195.001.
- ot_opcua_sabotage: none missing; two partials declared.
- The matrix prints these as a second table, "techniques demonstrated by a storyline with no rule", beside the rule-declared table. The ATT&CK ids above should be checked against the ATT&CK version already used in coverage_layer.py (v14) before commit.

== 4. Generated ATT&CK matrix: eval/attack/technique_matrix.py ==
Inputs:
- coverage_layer.load_rules(), plus a direct read of each rule's siem.threshold, window_seconds, group_by, distinct_field and companion_of, and whether its detection uses outside_hours.
- reg.ALL.
- The artefact eval/adversarial/out/scenario_matrix.latest.json. scenario_matrix gains an inputs_fingerprint (sha256 over the rule files, the oracle files and the eval source list), and technique_matrix refuses a stale artefact. This avoids re-running about 270 WS-8-graded variants twice in the gate. A --recompute flag runs scenario_matrix itself.

Per (framework, technique) row, with a per-rule sub-row:
- rule_exists: bool.
- fires_on_storyline: the list of (storyline, step) where the rule fired in the BASELINE grade (observed from fired, not read from the oracle). A companion rule is silent at baseline by design, so for companions the cell is "fires in variants", taken from the new rows[*].fired_pairs.
- survives_mutation: per (rule, storyline), over variants where the rule fired at baseline, each cell is survived, evaded_declared or evaded_unexpected.
  - evaded_declared is the evasion a rule's own YAML predicts:
    - volume / pacing / loss for any threshold rule;
    - distribution for group_by src_endpoint.ip, hostname or distinct src_ip;
    - identity for group_by actor;
    - timing/to_business_hours for any outside_hours rule.
  - Everything else is evaded_unexpected.
- Roll-up per technique.
- The demonstrated-undetected table from the oracle gap.attack_technique entries.
- Outputs: eval/attack/out/technique_matrix.json and .md, both deterministic (sorted keys, no timestamps). Optionally also a Navigator layer coloured declared / exercised / survives, as a v2 of coverage_layer.

Gate (exit 1), all from code:
1. Every rule with mitre.technique T is exercised (baseline fire, or companion fire in a variant) by at least one storyline. Otherwise "rule X (technique T) is exercised by no storyline".
2. Every technique id declared by any rule is exercised by at least one rule that fired.
3. Every rule has a mitre: block, or is in the closed table NO_TECHNIQUE_WAIVERS. After landing that table holds only agent_tool_call_burst, with its reason.
4. Closed UNEXERCISED_WAIVERS dict, empty after all six storylines land. A stale waiver (an entry whose rule is now exercised) also fails, the same pattern as oracle_consistency._ACCEPTED.
5. Ratchet against eval/attack/technique_matrix.baseline.json:
   - a survived to evaded cell fails;
   - an evaded to survived cell fails as a stale baseline, so improvements must be committed;
   - a new evaded_unexpected cell fails until it is investigated or baselined with a reason.
   The baseline file is the seam to the per-technique score ratchet planned elsewhere. This step creates it for survival cells only.
6. Determinism: the canonical JSON is byte-identical across two runs.

== 5. Harness changes needed so the new storylines are measured, not no-op'd ==
- mutate_generic adapters:
  - get/set_src_ip for cef (src=), db_audit (ipAddress), opcua_audit (clientAddress), sysmon (SourceIp) and inventory_diff (ip);
  - get/set_actor for cef (suser), db_audit (user), opcua_audit (clientUserId) and sysmon (User);
  - set_time also rewrites db_audit "timestamp", inventory_diff "seen_at" and k8s "requestReceivedTimestamp".
  test_mutation_adapters.py proves every adapter moves the PARSED field, not just the raw one, for every source_type used by any registered storyline. This may change existing infra_takeover numbers; if so, re-baseline and publish it as a correction, like the 2026-10-02 OPC UA grader-artefact correction.
- New static variants:
  - timing/to_business_hours and timing/to_night: shift the whole stream to the next weekday 10:30 UTC or 03:00 UTC, a pure shift that preserves spacing;
  - pacing/jitter_pct_50: +/-50% spacing, which defeats the beacon CV<=0.25 rule analytically, because uniform jitter j gives CV = j/sqrt(3), so evasion occurs above j=0.433;
  - distribution/hostname_rotate_all: rotate WorkstationName per event. This tests whether common_bruteforce_sourceless can be bypassed by a spoofed workstation name. I expect it can, but that is unverified.
- scenario_matrix: rows gain fired_pairs and rules_lost, additive; collateral logic honours oracle step_dependencies; the selfcheck is unchanged.
- oracle_consistency: new finding kinds forbidden_rule_fired and campaign_mismatch, with the same _ACCEPTED / stale-waiver mechanism.
- ScenarioDef: optional negatives=((name, builder, must_not_fire_ids), ...), defaulting to ().
- evasion_search: it iterates reg.ALL, so it covers the new burst steps automatically. It does not model periodicity, so add periodicity.max_cv to _rule_params and an analytic jitter prediction, or mark the beacon step "searched: false, reason: periodic rule". Do whichever the first run requires.

== 6. Build order ==
1. All six oracles plus provenance blocks, committed first.
2. The adapter and variant work plus test_mutation_adapters.
3. The builders and decoys.
4. Reconcile each storyline with oracle_consistency and record every finding.
5. technique_matrix plus its tests plus the baseline.
6. run_all_tests.sh wiring.
7. SSOT.md and CHANGELOG.md rows that report per-scenario numbers, not a pooled one.
positive_and_negative_controls: Existing 3 storylines unchanged after the adapter work, apart from any k8s/db/inventory timestamp correction; for each affected storyline the delta is reported as a correction rather than silently re-baselined.

POSITIVE: each of the six storylines parses strictly on its real parsers (run_chain strict=True; parse_expected=False only for mail_gateway and m365_audit). Each is deterministic (same seed gives byte-identical canonical output) and structure-varying (seeds 7/11/13/17 differ in at least one of counts, addresses, accounts, hosts).
NEGATIVE: scenario integrity fails loudly if a parse_expected step is dropped (disable_parser hook) and if a declared-gap source starts parsing.

POSITIVE: common_after_hours_admin fires in ransomware (23:46 UTC). NEGATIVE: the same rule stays silent on insider_exfil (Tue 10:30 UTC, must_not_fire) and also on its in-hours twin. The pair proves the time predicate is exercised in both directions.

NEGATIVE inside the oracle: must_not_fire checks, so a stray rule firing is reported as a finding. They include common_bruteforce on the slow spray, common_beaconing on irregular exfil, ot_config_change on the PumpEnable write, ot_modbus_unauthorized_write (high) on the forged-ticket write and common_bruteforce_by_account on the proxy-pool logins.

NEGATIVE twins at the boundary, each differing from its attack by exactly one asserted attribute: 19 reads vs 20, 49 burst calls vs 50, 7 vs 8 distinct IPs, 5 vs 6 beacons. Each must not fire its rule. A paired POSITIVE control proves the same builder with the attribute restored does fire it, so a silent harness cannot pass.

STALE-GAP tripwire (positive for the reconciler): cloud_iam_abuse.console_stuffing and the insider in-hours step are declared gaps; test_storylines_wide patches the oracle in memory to expect common_password_spray at the step and asserts reconcile reports DECORATIVE. This proves the reconciler can say no on the new storylines.

Oracle provenance: the test fails if any rule file's normalised description/detection/siem hash differs from the one recorded in the oracle's provenance block. Negative control: a temp copy of a rule with a changed threshold makes the test fail.

Mutation adapters: for every source used, set_src_ip/set_actor/set_time change the PARSED event field (positive). A source with no adapter returns False and the variant is reported N/A, never a pass (negative). The timing/to_business_hours variant turns ot_write_outside_maintenance dark but not ot_opcua_write_unauthorized_node on ot_opcua_sabotage, reproducing the 2026-10-01 OPC UA in-hours finding as a matrix cell.

Matrix gate POSITIVE: the real repo passes with only the agent_tool_call_burst no-technique waiver. NEGATIVE, injected in a temp rules directory: (a) a rule with technique T9999 and no storyline makes the gate exit 1; (b) a rule with no mitre block and no waiver exits 1; (c) a waiver for a rule that is exercised exits 1 as stale; (d) flipping one baseline cell from survived to evaded exits 1; (e) corrupting the artefact inputs_fingerprint is rejected as stale. The matrix is byte-identical across two runs.

Observed-vs-declared: a unit test removes a rule from reg.ALL expectations so that the matrix's fires_on_storyline disagrees with the oracle, and asserts the mismatch is surfaced. This stops the matrix from simply echoing the oracle.

Decoys: attack-disjoint entities give campaign_decoy_contamination 0.0 (positive). The same decoy retargeted onto an attack entity gives a value above 0 (negative), reusing the test_scenario_harness._with_decoys pattern.
acceptance: scenario_registry.ALL has 9 storylines (3 existing + 6 new) and python eval/twin/oracle_consistency.py exits 0 for all nine with no unrecorded finding. Every finding on a new storyline is either fixed or sits in _ACCEPTED with a dated reason, and any stale waiver fails.

python eval/adversarial/scenario_matrix.py --seed 7 exits 0: each new storyline has baseline TPR 1.0 over its non-gap steps and its shift_1h positive control passes. A loss variant turns a step dark (negative control). Zero storylines have all-N/A variants.

python eval/adversarial/evasion_search.py --seed 7 exits 0 with measured equal to predicted on every searched burst step. Any step it cannot model is reported searched:false with a reason, never silently agreed.

python eval/attack/technique_matrix.py exits 0. All 35 rules are exercised by a storyline (companions via variants). Every declared technique is exercised. The only waiver is agent_tool_call_burst (no technique). The ratchet baseline is committed.
The gate demonstrably goes red when any rule or technique loses its exercising storyline (the injected-rule control in test_technique_matrix.py passes).
Every gap step in the six oracles has attack_technique and reason; the missing-rule register matches section 3 exactly, and the matrix prints the demonstrated-undetected table.

test_storylines_wide.py, test_mutation_adapters.py and test_technique_matrix.py are wired into run_all_tests.sh, are accepted by tools/check_test_wiring.py, and the full ./run_all_tests.sh is green. Run it after the current gate finishes, not during it.
Per-scenario robustness is published (never a pooled number) in SSOT.md and CHANGELOG.md with the MISSING-rule register. A drop in the pooled mutation_robustness is stated as expected, not hidden.
Same-seed runs of storylines and the matrix are byte-identical; the six builders use no wall clock and no network; stdlib plus PyYAML only (PyYAML already used by report.py and coverage_layer.py).
risks: First-run reconciliation WILL disagree somewhere (the oracles are intent-first). Each decorative / unexpected / stale-gap result is a finding to fix or record, and the temptation to edit the oracle to match observed output must be resisted. Expect the campaign_membership expectation on the multi-entity chains to be the most likely mismatch.

The adapter completion can change the existing storylines' mutation results: set_time on k8s requestReceivedTimestamp probably makes infra_takeover time-shift variants real where they were partial no-ops. Treat it as a measured correction.

evasion_search does not model periodicity or workstation-keyed grouping, so the beacon, sourceless and hostname-rotate cells can produce false disagreements. Choose between extending the model and marking steps unsearched, and check by running before wiring into the gate.
Gate runtime grows about 3x (9 storylines x about 30 variants x WS-8 grading). Mitigation: technique_matrix reuses the scenario_matrix artefact with a fingerprint check instead of recomputing.

Companion rules fire only in variants, so their exercised status depends on the new fired_pairs rows. A variant list change could silently unexercise them; test_technique_matrix pins the companion rows.
The gate is red on first commit unless all six storylines land together; staged landing needs a populated UNEXERCISED_WAIVERS table that is then emptied.

Several oracles encode plausible-but-unverified ATT&CK ids for gap steps (T1074.001, T1565.001, T1114.003, T1562.008, T1087.004). A wrong id would be a documentation lie; verify against ATT&CK v14 before commit.

Provenance 'authored before run' cannot be mechanically proven; the rule-hash pin and commit-order convention only reduce, not remove, the self-authoring bias. A third-party labelled corpus remains the real fix (outside this step).

Sector differences: active_directory defaults to sector bank while windows_eventlog is common. Bank-scoped rules and AD-fed storylines can interact unexpectedly (this is why bank rules are driven only through db_audit).
The working tree is uncommitted and a gate is running, so file contents may move; the builders must be written against the on-disk state at implementation time.

mail_gateway and m365_audit are invented source_type names for chained gaps. They must be documented as 'no parser, by design' so they are not mistaken for planned parsers; the dead-letter integrity check requires exactly that count.
needs_owner_decision: WS-8 ADR-009/010 (tracks never merge): this design does not touch them. Decide whether the read-side campaign view (docs/proposals/2026-10-01-ws8-campaign-view.md is still a proposal) is the graded unit via the new oracle campaign_membership key, or whether pivoting chains are graded only on per-track incidents. Only the first lets a pivoting attack count as one campaign.

CloudTrail ConsoleLogin Failure is parsed as activity_id 1 / status Failure, so no brute-force or spray rule can see failed AWS console logins. Treat it as a parser bug to fix (the stale-gap tripwire then flips the oracle) or as the documented mapping to keep. The storyline records it as a gap either way.
agent_tool_call_burst has no mitre: block, deliberately. Tag it (which technique or ATLAS id?) or keep a permanent, reasoned NO_TECHNIQUE waiver in the matrix gate.

Whether the matrix gate fails hard immediately when a rule is unexercised, or starts warn-only until all six storylines land; and whether a first-run oracle disagreement is accepted into oracle_consistency._ACCEPTED or fixed in the product.

Declared-evadable policy: is evasion by shifting activity into business hours (after-hours and maintenance-window rules) classified as by-design 'evaded_declared', or as a defect to close with another rule, as ot_opcua_write_unauthorized_node did?

Priority of the source types that these storylines declare as chained gaps (mail gateway, M365 audit, a process-launch anomaly rule, a class-1001 file rule, a CloudTrail IAM/anomaly rule): the register in section 3 is a backlog, but nothing builds them in this step.

Whether the new storylines enter the frozen baseline contract (eval/twin/baseline.json, Phase 3.5 delta report) or stay in the separate scenario_matrix / technique_matrix lane, which is the intended design.

wrong_claims: Core inventory claims verified true: 35 rule files; exactly 16 are in no oracle (agent_destructive_command, agent_tool_call_burst, bank_db_priv_esc, bank_mass_card_read, common_after_hours_admin, common_beaconing, common_bruteforce_sourceless, common_impossible_travel, common_password_spray, common_rapid_account_lifecycle, ot_config_change, ot_modbus_unauthorized_write_ticketed, ot_new_device_on_segment, ot_new_engineering_connection, ot_opcua_write_unauthorized_node, ot_write_outside_maintenance). Only agent_tool_call_burst lacks a mitre block. I replayed the proposed event shapes through negative_controls.run_pipeline (real WS-2 to WS-4) and the rule predictions held: beaconing, password_spray, impossible_travel via cef, sourceless via AD 4625, lateral, rapid lifecycle, after-hours, dc_mass_vm_delete, bank_*, agent_*, all OT rules incl. the ticketed one, and the in-hours 4672 stays silent. All five companions (_by_account, dns_tunnel_by_domain, lateral_by_source, port_scan_by_target, dc_mass_vm_delete_by_source) do fire in existing-storyline variants. mail_gateway/m365_audit dict payloads dead-letter correctly.

WRONG: 'shift_* on infra_takeover's k8s step may be a silent partial no-op today' and 'adapter work may change existing infra_takeover numbers'. scenarios_extra._build_infra_takeover builds its k8s payload WITHOUT requestReceivedTimestamp (grep finds the field nowhere under eval/). None of cef, db_audit, sysmon, opcua_audit, inventory_diff is used by ai_to_ot, it_intrusion or infra_takeover, so the adapter completion cannot move any existing number. The 'report as a correction' branch is moot (the k8s fix only matters if the NEW supply_chain k8s payload includes the field).

WRONG: 'pacing/jitter_pct_50 defeats the beacon CV<=0.25 rule analytically, CV = j/sqrt(3), evasion above j=0.433'. That is the population CV of per-interval jitter. The engine (engine.py ~875 via hit_periodic) evaluates sample CV on 7 intervals and re-evaluates on every arrival (prefixes of 6, 7, 8 events), and the existing _jitter operator jitters each TIMESTAMP independently (interval variance doubles, threshold about 0.31). I simulated 8 beats at 60 s: with +/-50% per-timestamp jitter the rule STILL fires for about 17% of draws; with per-interval +/-50% mean sample CV is 0.264 so roughly half still fire. The variant would be seed-dependent, not a clean evasion. +/-100% gives about 2% still firing.
WRONG: 'three new mutation variants' -- the text lists four (timing/to_business_hours, timing/to_night, pacing/jitter_pct_50, distribution/hostname_rotate_all).

WRONG/overstated: 'time-of-day rules are never shown going silent'. mutate.py already has opcua_path_in_hours and the n8n after-hours rule exists in ai_to_ot; what is true is that no generic-lane storyline runs in hours.

WEAK CONTROL: insider_exfil exfil_upload 'must_not_fire common_beaconing (irregular and under 6 events)'. With 4 events the rule cannot fire on count alone (threshold 6), so the control never exercises the periodicity (CV) logic and cannot fail for the reason it claims.

WRONG: oracle_consistency can take new finding kinds 'with the same _ACCEPTED / stale-waiver mechanism' as-is. _key() only knows stale_gap, decorative/unexpected and falls through to item['from'], item['to'] for everything else, so forbidden_rule_fired and campaign_mismatch would raise KeyError; the 'seen' loop in reconcile() also hard-codes four kinds.

IMPRECISE: cloud_iam_abuse.iam_persistence is tagged T1098.001 for CreateUser + CreateAccessKey + AttachUserPolicy. CreateAccessKey is T1098.001, AttachUserPolicy is T1098.003, CreateUser is T1136.003; one id per three different techniques will mislabel the demonstrated-undetected table.

INCONSISTENT with existing oracles: the new oracles set incident_count to the 'honest' 0/1 (report._incident_membership_grade expects exactly incident_count incidents carrying the FULL chain), but oracle_it_intrusion.yaml declares incident_count 1 and SSOT row 17 records that WS-8 yields 4 incidents so incident_membership_ok=False at baseline. Two conventions would coexist across the 9 storylines and the pooled/per-scenario membership numbers would not be comparable.
missing: verify_subset_equivalence is not mentioned. test_scenario_harness.py:340 asserts evasion_search.verify_subset_equivalence(s, SEED) == [] for every reg.ALL storyline. evasion_search._detects scores a step on ONLY its own events. Single-event steps that depend on an earlier step (phishing_bec.foreign_login and cloud_iam_abuse.attacker_console_login, both common_impossible_travel which needs the victim_session event) fire on the full stream but NOT on the subset, so that existing test goes red. step_dependencies is only wired into scenario_matrix; evasion_search._detects/verify_subset_equivalence must pull in the dependency (context) steps' events too, or victim+attacker logins must be one step.

evasion_search WILL disagree on c2_beacon's loss axis, not just 'may'. _thin_step drops evenly spaced events, so removing 1 of 8 beats leaves a 120 s gap: sample CV about 0.31-0.33 > 0.25, so measured tolerated loss is 0 while _predict says n-T = 2. Mark the step searched:false ('periodic rule: thinning changes CV') or add a periodicity-aware loss model BEFORE wiring, and add periodicity.max_cv to _rule_params. (ip_k=2 and the 1200% stretch do agree.)

mutate_generic needs get/set_hostname adapters (active_directory/windows WorkstationName) for distribution/hostname_rotate_all; the adapter list in section 5 covers only src_ip, actor and time. Also evasion_search/scenario_matrix still treat set_src_ip/set_actor returning False as a silent no-op that reads as 'immune'; add a changed_events>0 assertion inside _search_spread (an unmodelled source passes vacuously where the rule is predicted immune).

technique_matrix survives_mutation does not say how to treat (a) loss/drop_<own step> for stateless single-event rules (every such rule x its own drop variant would be an evaded_unexpected cell and trip the ratchet; scenario_matrix already treats it as the negative control), (b) N/A variants (changed==0) vs not-fired, (c) the context-step dependency (drop_victim_session legitimately blinds impossible_travel).

The artefact guard is incomplete: eval/adversarial/out/ is gitignored, so scenario_matrix.latest.json does not exist on a fresh checkout and the fingerprint (rule files + oracle files + eval sources) does not cover seed or scenario subset. A 'scenario_matrix.py --scenario X' or '--seed 11' run writes the same default path and would be accepted. Record seed and the scenario-name list in the artefact and assert seed==7 and set==reg.BY_NAME in technique_matrix. Also place the technique_matrix stanza in run_all_tests.sh AFTER the scenario_matrix stanza (line ~501), not next to the eval/attack stanzas at ~443-449.

ScenarioDef.negatives needs a consumer: scenario_matrix/oracle_consistency do not run it and test_registry_and_integrity (test_scenario_harness.py:68) hard-codes the expected_sequence==steps check; specify where negatives are executed and that the 'attribute restored' positive twin shares the same builder code path.

Existing test_scenario_harness checks (decoy, matrix gate, evasion) loop over reg.ALL and some may embed 3-storyline assumptions; they need an audit when the registry grows to 9. Matrix gate runtime: grading 3 storylines over all variants took about 72 s here, so 9 storylines plus the extra variants is roughly 4-6 min on top of the current 774 s gate.

Section 3 'register' and the matrix list expected_rules by technique but the oracles also need the evidence.per_step, severity_band and cross_step_rule_ids blocks the grader reads (report._severity_band_check, _severity_confusion); for low-severity-only storylines (cloud_iam_abuse has one rule, the ticketed Modbus rule is level low with exposure_gate false) the dominant_band must be authored honestly or severity_band_ok will fail.

alert_order_ok: phishing_bec lists c2_beacon before victim_session, but the beacon alert fires only on the 6th beat (about 5 min in); the builder must stagger so first-alert times are monotone in expected_sequence order, or the new order metric fails at baseline.
critic_verdict.corrections: ["Keep the design; it is feasible and the firing/coverage claims are sound. Apply these fixes before implementation. (1) Drop the claim that existing storylines may shift; state that cef/db_audit/sysmon/opcua/inventory adapters affect only new storylines, and only add the k8s requestReceivedTimestamp rewrite if a new payload carries it. (2) Replace pacing/jitter_pct_50 with a per-timestamp jitter of +/-100% of the period (about 2% residual fire) or, better, bisect jitter in evasion_search against a measured boundary; drop the 'j/sqrt(3)=0.433' analytic prediction or re-derive it for per-timestamp jitter and sample CV over 6..n prefixes. (3) Extend evasion_search._detects and verify_subset_equivalence to include the oracle step_dependencies steps' events, else test_scenario_harness.py:340 fails on the two impossible_travel steps. (4) Mark c2_beacon searched:false (periodic rule) for the loss axis, or implement a periodicity-aware loss prediction, and only wire evasion_search into the gate after one clean run. (5) Make the exfil_upload beacon negative control meaningful: use 6+ irregular sysmon 3 events (CV > 0.25) so common_beaconing could fire on count but must not on regularity, paired with the existing 6-regular positive. (6) In oracle_consistency, generalise _key() and the 'seen' loop for forbidden_rule_fired and campaign_mismatch. (7) Pick ONE incident_count convention for all nine oracles (recommend: incident_count is the number of full-chain incidents WS-8 really produces today, with a comment, and leave it_intrusion's aspirational 1 flagged as the known membership_ok=False), and report it explicitly. (8) Split iam_persistence into per-event techniques (CreateAccessKey T1098.001, AttachUserPolicy T1098.003, CreateUser T1136.003) or use only the one the oracle step is about; verify all ids against ATT&CK v14 and the ICS ids already used by the OT rules. (9) technique_matrix: exclude loss/drop_<own step> and changed==0 variants from survive/evade cells, record seed + scenario list in the artefact and check them, order the stanza after scenario_matrix. (10) Add get/set_hostname adapters for hostname_rotate_all, and fix the text to four new variants. (11) Effort: the 56 h estimate omits the evasion_search periodic handling, the subset-equivalence change, the negatives consumer and 3-9 storyline test audit; revise to about 80 h.", "Verified-existing names used by the design (no change needed): scenario.ScenarioDef/ChainStepSpec/run_chain, scenario_registry.ALL/BY_NAME/get/load_oracle/run/grade, oracle_consistency.reconcile/_ACCEPTED/_companion_sibling, report._grade_chain/_real_detection/_incident_membership_grade, grade keys campaign_count/campaign_full_coverage/campaign_decoy_contamination, scenario_matrix.run_scenario/_selfcheck, mutate_generic.set_time/get_src_ip/variants_for/apply, evasion_search._rule_params/_predict/search_scenario, negative_controls._epoch_ms, test_scenario_harness._with_decoys, coverage_layer.load_rules, tools/check_test_wiring.py, services/ws8-correlation/campaigns.py and docs/proposals/2026-10-01-ws8-campaign-view.md (both uncommitted/untracked on disk), contracts/allowlists/opcua_authorized_nodes.yml (untracked, entries: [] as claimed). The frozen baseline (eval/twin/baseline.json, report.py chain) is not touched because new storylines stay in the scenario_matrix lane; no ratified WS-8 ADR-009/010 invariant is violated (campaign_membership is read-side via link_campaigns); the work stays zero-infra (memory bus, stdlib + PyYAML)."]
